topicBn: Alexander Pope — Mock-Heroic Epic & Neo-Classical Period (Hard)

options.D: “Child is the father of the man.”

options.A: The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock

explanationBn: ১৯৪৮ সালে সাহিত্যে নোবেলজয়ী আধুনিক কবি T.S. Eliot-এর সবচেয়ে বিখ্যাত কাব্যগ্রন্থ ‘The Waste Land’ (১৯২২)-এর প্রথম লাইন হলো “April is the cruellest month”।
source: ৪৫তম ও ৩৭তম বিসিএস

topicBn: W.B. Yeats — Irish Poet & Gitanjali Introduction (Medium)
stem: Which Irish Nobel Laureate poet wrote the introduction to Rabindranath Tagore’s English “Gitanjali” (Song Offerings) and authored “The Second Coming” and “The Lake Isle of Innisfree”?
explanationBn: আইরিশ জাতীয়তাবাদী কবি W.B. Yeats (১৯২৩ সালে নোবেলজয়ী) রবীন্দ্রনাথের ইংরেজি গীতাঞ্জলির ভূমিকা লিখেছিলেন; তাঁর বিখ্যাত কবিতা ‘The Second Coming’ (“Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold”), ‘Easter 1916’ এবং ‘Sailing to Byzantium’।
source: ৪৩তম ও ৪০তম বিসিএস

stem: What was the real name of George Orwell, the author of “Animal Farm”, “Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984)” and “Shooting an Elephant”?
explanationBn: George Orwell-এর প্রকৃত নাম Eric Arthur Blair; Mark Twain-এর প্রকৃত নাম Samuel Langhorne Clemens; এবং O. Henry-র প্রকৃত নাম William Sydney Porter।
source: ৪৪তম বিসিএস ও ব্যাংক পরীক্ষা

topicBn: Ernest Hemingway — The Old Man and the Sea (Medium)
stem: “Man is not made for defeat. A man can be destroyed but not defeated”—this famous line appears in which novella by American Nobel Laureate Ernest Hemingway?

options.B: The Old Man and the Sea (1952)

explanationBn: কিউবার বৃদ্ধ জেলে Santiago ও বিশাল Marlin মাছের সংগ্রাম নিয়ে রচিত Ernest Hemingway-র পুলিৎজার ও নোবেলজয়ী উপন্যাসিকা ‘The Old Man and the Sea’ (১৯৫২)-র অমর বাণী এটি।
source: ৪৬তম ও ৩৯তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Literary Terms — Soliloquy vs Dramatic Monologue vs Elegy (Hard)
stem: In drama, when a character speaks his or her inner thoughts aloud while alone on stage (such as Hamlet’s “To be, or not to be”), it is called a—
explanationBn: মঞ্চে একা থাকা অবস্থায় চরিত্রের নিজের মনের সাথে উচ্চস্বরে কথা বলাকে Soliloquy (স্বগতোক্তি) বলে; আর কবিতায় একজন বক্তা ও নীরব শ্রোতার উপস্থিতিতে একক বক্তৃতাকে Dramatic Monologue বলে।
source: ৪৫তম ও ৪১তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Old & Middle English — Geoffrey Chaucer & Canterbury Tales (Medium)
stem: Who is universally acclaimed as the “Father of English Poetry” (and the morning star of the Renaissance/Reformation is John Wycliffe) and what is his masterpiece?

options.A: Geoffrey Chaucer — “The Canterbury Tales” (written in Middle English)

explanationBn: চতুর্দশ শতাব্দীর কবি Geoffrey Chaucer-কে ‘Father of English Poetry’ এবং ‘Father of English Language’ বলা হয়; তাঁর শ্রেষ্ঠ কাব্যগ্রন্থ ‘The Canterbury Tales’। (অন্যদিকে অ্যাংলো-স্যাক্সন বা Old English যুগের মহাকাব্য হলো ‘Beowulf’ এবং বাইবেলের প্রথম ইংরেজি অনুবাদক John Wycliffe-কে Morning Star of the Reformation বলা হয়)।
source: ৪৩তম ও ৩৭তম বিসিএস

stem: Which group of 16th-century Elizabethan playwrights and pamphleteers educated at Oxford or Cambridge was known as the “University Wits”?

options.A: Christopher Marlowe, Thomas Kyd, Robert Greene, Thomas Nashe, George Peele, John Lyly, and Thomas Lodge (Note: William Shakespeare was NOT one of them!)
options.B: William Shakespeare, Ben Jonson, and Francis Bacon
options.C: John Milton, John Donne, and Andrew Marvell
options.D: John Dryden, Alexander Pope, and Jonathan Swift

explanationBn: অক্সফোর্ড (John Lyly, George Peele, Thomas Lodge) এবং কেমব্রিজ (Christopher Marlowe, Robert Greene, Thomas Nashe) বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ে শিক্ষিত ৬ জন নাট্যকার ও Thomas Kyd—এই ৭ জনকে একত্রে ‘University Wits’ বলা হয়। শেক্সপিয়ার বা বেন জনসন এর অন্তর্ভুক্ত ছিলেন না!
source: ৪৪তম ও ৩৮তম বিসিএস

stem: “All the world’s a stage, / And all the men and women merely players”—in which comedy of William Shakespeare does the melancholic character Jaques speak these lines?

options.A: As You Like It (spoken by Jaques in the Forest of Arden)

explanationBn: শেক্সপিয়ারের রোমান্টিক কমেডি ‘As You Like It’-এ বিষণ্ণ দার্শনিক চরিত্র Jaques মানুষের জীবনের ৭টি স্তরের বর্ণনা দিতে গিয়ে বলেন: “All the world’s a stage...”। (অন্যদিকে “Life’s but a walking shadow, a poor player” উক্তিটি ‘Macbeth’ ট্র্যাজেডির!)।
source: ৪৫তম ও ৩৬তম বিসিএস

topicBn: William Shakespeare — The Tempest & Measure for Measure (Medium)
stem: Which play is widely regarded as William Shakespeare’s “Swan Song” (his last standalone play), featuring the characters Prospero, Miranda, Ariel, and Caliban?
explanationBn: শেক্সপিয়ারের সর্বশেষ একক নাটক (Swan Song) হলো ‘The Tempest’ (১৬১১), যার প্রধান চরিত্র মিলানের ডিউক Prospero, তাঁর কন্যা Miranda, বায়বীয় আত্মা Ariel এবং দানব Caliban। এ নাটকের বিখ্যাত উক্তি: “O brave new world, that has such people in’t!”
source: ৪১তম ও ৩৭তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Jacobean Period — John Webster & The Duchess of Malfi (Hard)
stem: Who wrote the famous Jacobean revenge tragedies “The Duchess of Malfi” and “The White Devil”, containing the line “Cover her face; mine eyes dazzle: she died young”?
explanationBn: জ্যাকোবিয়ান যুগের অন্যতম শ্রেষ্ঠ ট্র্যাজেডি নাট্যকার John Webster রচনা করেন ‘The Duchess of Malfi’ (চরিত্র: Bosola, Ferdinand, Duchess) এবং ‘The White Devil’।
source: ৪৪তম বিসিএস ইংলিশ লিটারেচার

topicBn: Puritan Age — John Milton’s Areopagitica & Elegies (Hard)
stem: Which prose work by the epic poet John Milton is a passionate philosophical defense of “freedom of the press and free speech”, and what is his pastoral elegy on the death of his friend Edward King?
explanationBn: মিল্টনের বিখ্যাত গদ্যগ্রন্থ ‘Areopagitica’ সংবাদপত্র ও বাক-স্বাধীনতার পক্ষে রচিত এবং বন্ধু Edward King-এর মৃত্যুতে রচিত শোককাব্য হলো ‘Lycidas’। (উল্লেখ্য: Adonais লিখেছেন Shelley কীটসের মৃত্যুতে; এবং In Memoriam লিখেছেন Tennyson বন্ধু Arthur Hallam-এর মৃত্যুতে)।
source: ৪৩তম ও ৩৮তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Restoration Period — William Congreve & Comedy of Manners (Hard)
stem: Who is the master of Restoration “Comedy of Manners”, famous for plays such as “The Way of the World” and “Love for Love”?
explanationBn: রেস্টোরেশন যুগে উচ্চবিত্ত সমাজের কৃত্রিম আচার-আচরণকে ব্যঙ্গ করে রচিত ‘Comedy of Manners’-এর শ্রেষ্ঠ নাট্যকার William Congreve; তাঁর শ্রেষ্ঠ নাটক ‘The Way of the World’ (১৭০০ — চরিত্র: Mirabell ও Millamant)।
source: ৪৫তম বিসিএস ও পিএসসি নন-ক্যাডার

topicBn: Augustan / Neoclassical Age — Daniel Defoe & Jonathan Swift (Medium)
stem: “Man Friday” is a famous character in which adventure novel by Daniel Defoe, and what are the four voyages in Jonathan Swift’s satire “Gulliver’s Travels”?

options.A: Novel: “Robinson Crusoe” (1719); Voyages in Gulliver’s Travels: Lilliput (dwarfs), Brobdingnag (giants), Laputa, and the land of the Houyhnhnms
options.B: Novel: “Treasure Island”; Voyages: Utopia and Atlantis

explanationBn: Daniel Defoe-এর ‘Robinson Crusoe’ (১৭১৯) উপন্যাসের বিখ্যাত চরিত্র ‘Man Friday’। আর Jonathan Swift-এর রাজনৈতিক ব্যঙ্গাত্মক উপন্যাস ‘Gulliver’s Travels’ (১৭২৬)-এর ৪টি খণ্ড হলো: Lilliput, Brobdingnag, Laputa এবং Houyhnhnms (বুদ্ধিমান ঘোড়াদের দেশ)।
source: ৪০তম ও ৩৫তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Pre-Romantic / Graveyard Poets — Thomas Gray’s Elegy (Medium)
stem: “Where ignorance is bliss, ’tis folly to be wise” and “Full many a flower is born to blush unseen”—these immortal lines are from which poem by Thomas Gray?

options.A: Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard (and Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College)
options.B: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

explanationBn: Graveyard Poet নামে পরিচিত Thomas Gray-এর ‘Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard’ (১৭৫১) কবিতার বিখ্যাত চরণ: “The paths of glory lead but to the grave” এবং “Full many a flower is born to blush unseen”।
source: ৪৪তম ও ৩৬তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Romantic Period — Lord Byron & Don Juan (Medium)
stem: Which Romantic poet is known as the “Rebel Poet” of English literature, created the “Byronic Hero”, and wrote the epic satire “Don Juan” and “Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage”?
explanationBn: লর্ড বায়রনকে (Lord Byron) ইংরেজি সাহিত্যের ‘Rebel Poet’ (বিদ্রোহী কবি) বলা হয় (আর Shelley-কে বলা হয় Revolutionary Poet)। বায়রনের বিখ্যাত রচনা: Don Juan, Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage, এবং কাব্য: “She Walks in Beauty”।
source: ৪২তম ও ৩৮তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Victorian Period — Thomas Hardy’s Wessex Novels (Hard)
stem: Which Victorian novelist created the fictional region of “Wessex” in pessimistic novels such as “Tess of the d’Urbervilles”, “The Return of the Native”, and “The Mayor of Casterbridge”?
explanationBn: ভিক্টোরিয়ান যুগের হতাশাবাদী (Pessimistic) ঔপন্যাসিক ও কবি Thomas Hardy-এর বিখ্যাত উপন্যাসগুলো হলো: Tess of the d’Urbervilles, Far from the Madding Crowd, The Return of the Native, The Mayor of Casterbridge এবং Jude the Obscure।
source: ৪৫তম ও ৪১তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Victorian Women Novelists — Brontë Sisters & George Eliot (Hard)
stem: Match the Victorian masterpieces with their female authors: (1) “Jane Eyre”, (2) “Wuthering Heights”, and (3) “Silas Marner / Middlemarch”.

options.A: (1) Charlotte Brontë, (2) Emily Brontë (character: Heathcliff), and (3) George Eliot (pen name of Mary Ann Evans)
options.B: (1) Jane Austen, (2) Charlotte Brontë, and (3) Virginia Woolf
options.C: (1) Emily Brontë, (2) Anne Brontë, and (3) Elizabeth Barrett Browning
options.D: (1) George Eliot, (2) Jane Austen, and (3) Emily Dickinson

explanationBn: Charlotte Brontë লিখেছেন ‘Jane Eyre’; তাঁর বোন Emily Brontë লিখেছেন তাঁর একমাত্র উপন্যাস ‘Wuthering Heights’ (যার কেন্দ্রীয় চরিত্র Heathcliff ও Catherine); এবং Mary Ann Evans ‘George Eliot’ ছদ্মনামে লিখেছেন ‘Silas Marner’, ‘Adam Bede’ ও ‘Middlemarch’।
source: ৪৬তম ও ৪০তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Modern Period — T.S. Eliot & The Waste Land (Hard)
stem: “April is the cruellest month, breeding / Lilacs out of the dead land”—this famous opening line belongs to which landmark modernist poem that won its author the 1948 Nobel Prize in Literature?
explanationBn: আধুনিক ইংরেজি কবিতার শ্রেষ্ঠ নিদর্শন T.S. Eliot-এর ‘The Waste Land’ (১৯২২, কবি Ezra Pound-কে উৎসর্গীকৃত)। এলিয়টের অন্যান্য বিখ্যাত রচনা: The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock, The Hollow Men এবং কাব্যনাট্য Murder in the Cathedral।
source: ৪৪তম ও ৩৭তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Modern Drama — George Bernard Shaw & Drama of Ideas (Medium)
stem: Who wrote the famous satirical plays “Arms and the Man”, “Man and Superman”, “Pygmalion”, and “Saint Joan”, and received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1925?

options.A: George Bernard Shaw (G.B. Shaw — Father of Modern English Drama)

explanationBn: আইরিশ বংশোদ্ভূত নাট্যকার G.B. Shaw-কে আধুনিক ইংরেজি ‘Drama of Ideas’-এর জনক বলা হয়। ‘Arms and the Man’ নাটকে তিনি যুদ্ধ ও রোমান্টিসিজমকে ব্যঙ্গ করেছেন (চরিত্র: Bluntschli ও Raina) এবং ‘Pygmalion’ নাটক থেকে পরবর্তীতে ‘My Fair Lady’ চলচ্চিত্র নির্মিত হয়।
source: ৪৫তম, ৪১তম ও ৩৫তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Post-Colonial & World Literature — Chinua Achebe, Gabriel García Márquez & Toni Morrison (Hard)
stem: Match the following world literature classics with their Nobel/renowned authors: (1) “Things Fall Apart”, (2) “One Hundred Years of Solitude”, and (3) “Beloved”.

options.A: (1) Chinua Achebe (Nigeria — character: Okonkwo), (2) Gabriel García Márquez (Colombia — Magic Realism), and (3) Toni Morrison (USA)
options.B: (1) Wole Soyinka, (2) Pablo Neruda, and (3) Ernest Hemingway
options.C: (1) Nelson Mandela, (2) Jorge Luis Borges, and (3) Alice Walker
options.D: (1) Ngũgĩ wa Thiong’o, (2) Salman Rushdie, and (3) Virginia Woolf

explanationBn: আফ্রিকান সাহিত্যের জনক নাইজেরিয়ার Chinua Achebe রচনা করেন ‘Things Fall Apart’ (১৯৫৮); কলম্বিয়ার নোবেলজয়ী লেখক Gabriel García Márquez জাদুবাস্তবতা (Magic Realism) শৈলীতে রচনা করেন ‘One Hundred Years of Solitude’; এবং প্রথম কৃষ্ণাঙ্গ নারী নোবেলজয়ী মার্কিন লেখিকা Toni Morrison রচনা করেন ‘Beloved’ ও ‘The Bluest Eye’।
source: ৪৬তম ও ৪৩তম বিসিএস

topicBn: Elizabethan Literature — Shakespeare's Four Great Tragedies (Critical)
stem: Which of the following represents William Shakespeare's four great tragedies arranged in correct chronological order of composition?
explanationBn: The mnemonic H-O-L-M (Hamlet -> Othello -> King Lear -> Macbeth) captures Shakespeare's four supreme tragedies written between 1601 and 1606.
source: 45th & 40th BCS English Literature

stem: In John Donne's metaphysical masterpiece 'A Valediction: Forbidding Mourning', the souls of the two separated lovers are famously compared to:

options.B: The twin compasses used by a draftsman
options.C: A bird and its migratory flight path
options.D: Sun and moon in perpetual orbit

explanationBn: This is the most celebrated metaphysical conceit in English literature: Donne compares his and his wife's souls to the two stiff legs of a draughtsman's compass (one fixed in the center while the other leans and roams).
source: 44th & 38th BCS Literature

topicBn: Romantic Period — Preface to Lyrical Ballads (Critical)
stem: The manifesto of English Romanticism, 'Preface to Lyrical Ballads' (1800), wherein poetry is defined as 'the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings', was authored by:
explanationBn: While 'Lyrical Ballads' (1798) was co-published by Wordsworth (19 poems) and Coleridge (4 poems including Rime of the Ancient Mariner), the famous 'Preface' was written solely by William Wordsworth in the second edition (1800).
source: 46th & 41st BCS Literature

stem: The aesthetic concept of 'Negative Capability'—the capacity to exist in uncertainties, mysteries, and doubts without any irritable reaching after fact and reason—was coined by:
explanationBn: John Keats introduced 'Negative Capability' in a letter to his brothers in December 1817, citing Shakespeare as the prime example of an author possessing this quality.
source: 45th & 37th BCS Literature

stem: Robert Browning is pre-eminently celebrated in Victorian literature for mastering which poetic form?

options.B: Dramatic Monologue (seen in 'My Last Duchess' and 'Fra Lippo Lippi')

explanationBn: Robert Browning perfected the Dramatic Monologue, where a single fictional speaker addresses a silent listener at a moment of emotional crisis, unintentionally revealing their true character (e.g. Duke of Ferrara in 'My Last Duchess').
source: 44th & 41st BCS Literature

stem: The Victorian masterpiece 'Middlemarch' was written under the male pen name 'George Eliot' by the female novelist:
explanationBn: George Eliot was the pseudonym of Mary Ann Evans (1819–1880), author of 'Middlemarch', 'Silas Marner', 'The Mill on the Floss', and 'Adam Bede'.
source: 43rd & 36th BCS Literature

topicBn: Modernist Poetry — T.S. Eliot & The Waste Land (Critical)
stem: The modernist landmark poem 'The Waste Land' (1922) by T.S. Eliot opens with which immortal line?

options.A: 'Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold'
options.B: 'April is the cruellest month, breeding / Lilacs out of the dead land'
options.C: 'Let us go then, you and I, / When the evening is spread out against the sky'
options.D: 'Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?'

explanationBn: 'The Waste Land' (dedicated to Ezra Pound, 'il miglior fabbro') begins with the famous line 'April is the cruellest month...'. Line A is by W.B. Yeats, Line C is from Eliot's 'The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock'.
source: 45th & 42nd BCS Literature

topicBn: Modernist Fiction — Stream of Consciousness & Joyce (Critical)
stem: Which 1922 modernist novel depicts a single day (June 16, 1904 — Bloomsday) in the life of Leopold Bloom in Dublin using the Stream of Consciousness technique?

options.A: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man
options.D: The Great Gatsby (by F. Scott Fitzgerald)

explanationBn: 'Ulysses' by James Joyce chronicles June 16, 1904 in Dublin across 18 episodes paralleling Homer's Odyssey, celebrated globally as Bloomsday.
source: 44th & 39th BCS Literature

topicBn: Irish Revival & W.B. Yeats — Nobel Prize (Critical)
stem: W.B. Yeats, who wrote the Introduction to Rabindranath Tagore's English 'Song Offerings' (Gitanjali) in 1912, was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in:
explanationBn: Rabindranath Tagore received the Nobel Prize in 1913, while his close admirer and Irish poet W.B. Yeats received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1923. George Bernard Shaw received it in 1925.
source: 46th & 40th BCS Literature

topicBn: Modern Drama — George Bernard Shaw & Pygmalion (Critical)
stem: In G.B. Shaw's satirical drama 'Pygmalion' (1913), Professor Henry Higgins wagers that he can transform which Cockney flower girl into a duchess?
explanationBn: Eliza Doolittle is the Cockney flower girl taught phonetics and etiquette by Professor Henry Higgins in Shaw's 'Pygmalion' (adapted into the musical 'My Fair Lady').
source: 45th & 38th BCS Literature

topicBn: American Literature — Ernest Hemingway & Nobel Prize (Critical)
stem: Ernest Hemingway was awarded the 1954 Nobel Prize in Literature primarily for his mastery of narrative art demonstrated in which novella?

options.C: The Old Man and the Sea (featuring Cuban fisherman Santiago)

explanationBn: 'The Old Man and the Sea' (1952) won the Pulitzer Prize in 1953 and was cited as the principal reason for Hemingway receiving the 1954 Nobel Prize in Literature. Central quote: 'A man can be destroyed but not defeated.'
source: 44th & 37th BCS Literature

topicBn: Epic Poetry — John Milton's Paradise Lost (Critical)
stem: In John Milton's 12-book epic 'Paradise Lost' (1667), what stated objective does the poet set out to achieve in Book I?

options.A: 'To depict the glorious triumph of human ambition'
options.B: 'To justify the ways of God to men'
options.C: 'To expose the theological corruption of the clergy'
options.D: 'To mourn the tragic downfall of England\'s commonwealth'

explanationBn: Milton declares his grand epic purpose in Book I (line 26): 'That to the heighth of this great Argument / I may assert Eternal Providence, / And justifie the wayes of God to men.'
source: 46th & 35th BCS Literature

stem: Jonathan Swift's biting political satire 'Gulliver's Travels' (1726) describes Lemuel Gulliver's voyages to four distinct lands in which exact order?

options.A: Lilliput, Brobdingnag, Laputa, and the Land of the Houyhnhnms

explanationBn: Gulliver's four voyages: 1. Lilliput (tiny people, 6 inches), 2. Brobdingnag (giants), 3. Laputa (flying island of eccentric philosophers), 4. Land of Houyhnhnms (rational talking horses ruling barbaric human-like Yahoos).

topicBn: Romantic Odes — Shelley's Ode to the West Wind (Critical)
stem: Percy Bysshe Shelley concludes his famous poem 'Ode to the West Wind' with which optimistic rhetorical prophecy?

options.A: 'Beauty is truth, truth beauty,—that is all'
options.B: 'If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?'
options.C: 'Water, water, everywhere, / Nor any drop to drink'
options.D: 'The world is too much with us; late and soon'

explanationBn: Shelley's final trumpet of prophecy in 'Ode to the West Wind' is: 'O, Wind, / If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?' (Option A is Keats's Ode on a Grecian Urn).

topicBn: Literary Terms — Soliloquy vs Aside vs Monologue (Critical)
stem: A dramatic speech made by a character alone on stage, revealing their inmost thoughts directly to the audience, is termed a:
explanationBn: A 'Soliloquy' is spoken when a character is alone on stage (e.g. Hamlet's 'To be, or not to be'). An 'Aside' is spoken while others are on stage but presumed not to hear. A 'Dramatic Monologue' is spoken to an implied silent listener.
source: 44th & 36th BCS Literature
